sentence: This project studies how DNA differences change a gene in endothelial cells and how that gene can affect artery walls to cause cardiovascular disease.
This project studies how transient receptor potential vanilloid channels are opened by molecules and what one of them does in developing neurons and immune cells.
This project studies how serotonin in early development affects parvalbumin interneurons in the prefrontal cortex and cognitive behavior.
This project builds computer tools that screen large libraries of compounds and predict whether they can cross the blood-brain barrier.
This project builds an imaging method that measures blood flow in the heart and blood vessels of early mouse embryos.
This project builds an assay that follows gene expression, cell death and infection in single lung cells infected with influenza virus.
This project tests whether a computer tool that uses features from CT images can better judge cancer risk in pulmonary nodules.
This project studies what causes damage and scarring of the urethral wall in urethral stricture, including repeated interventions and microorganisms in urine.
This project tries to find ways to deliver therapeutic material to skeletal muscle using fusogenic proteins that are already active in the body.
This project studies how exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons near Superfund sites may contribute to preterm birth, using the placenta.
This project supports nonhuman primate research programs that aim to improve human health.
This project provides equipment that measures eye structure and visual function in living rodents to study retinal and other eye diseases.
This project studies how three compounds work against HIV that has become resistant to the drug lenacapavir.
This project studies how metformin changes signaling pathways during early myelin development in mice.
This project studies how reprogramming factors help supporting cells and hair cells regenerate in mice.
This project studies metastatic breast cancer to find genetic weak points and causes of endocrine resistance.
This project studies why mice whose hexokinase 1 enzyme cannot bind mitochondria develop heart failure and damaged endothelial cells.
This project provides mouse bone marrow stem cells, muscle cells and services such as mitochondrial function assays for related research projects.
This project uses long-read sequencing to find which retroelement and host factors affect the outcomes of retrotransposition.
This project studies how opioid receptor activation reverses epigenetic changes and protects retinal ganglion cells in glaucoma.
